title: tidystata
text: English tidystata 把 Stata 风格的数据探索和整理带到 R 中：查看变量、汇总统计、列频数表、生成新变量。变量可以用 tidyselect 方式选择，分组计算用 .。结果都是普通的数据表，可以继续用 R 的常用工具筛选、合并和作图。

title: tidystata
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("socimh/tidystata")

title: tidystata
code: library(tidystata) library(dplyr)

what: findit()：查找 Stata 命令对应的 R 代码
title: tidystata
text: 单独查询命令（如 findit(egen)）返回整个命令族，默认显示最多五种操作。具体查询（如 findit("egen rowmean")）返回一个明确的推荐；含义不明确时保留最多十个相关候选项。print(n = Inf) 展开已返回的结果；查询命令族可浏览更广的操作。同一任务优先推荐 tidystata，其次是 tidyverse，最后是其他包或 base R。可以用逗号添加变量名或提示，例如 findit(tab, sex, region) 或 findit(tab, gen)。在中文环境下运行 R 时，条目说明会显示为中文。全部条目按主题列在从 Stata 到 R中。 也可以输入 Stata 文本：findit(`tab sex region`, row) 和 findit("tab sex region, row") 会用指定变量生成相同的行百分比示例。 查询 -file 中的一条命令时，可选中文本后运行 Find Stata equivalent 插件（findit_selection()），或复制文本后运行 findit_clip()。 两者均在控制台显示结果，分别需要可选的 rstudioapi 和 clipr 包。
code: findit("reg, robust") #> # Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors [fixest] #> Stata: regress y x1 x2, robust #> R:     fixest::feols(y ~ x1 + x2, data = data, vcov = "hetero") #> # Note: Match fixest covariance small-sample corrections and singleton handling with Stata; the same formula does not guarantee identical standard errors or retained observations. #>  #> # 16 broader regress examples. Browse the family: findit(regress) findit("egen rowmean") #> # Average available values across columns [tidystata] #> Stata: egen z = rowmean(x y) #> R:     mutate(data, z = row_mean(x, y)) #>  #> # 70 broader egen examples. Browse the family: findit(egen)

what: tab()、tab1() 和 tab2()：比较频数表
title: tidystata
text: 用 lifeexp 中的地区和一个新类别作比较：预期寿命是否达到 70 岁。region:lexp_70 选择这两列。 tab() 统计每种实际出现的组合的频数，并给出百分比。 tab1() 返回一个命名列表，为每个变量分别生成频数表。 tab2() 将联合频数排列成交叉表，地区为行，预期寿命类别为列。 也可以对连续变量制表。当不同取值较多时，用 print_interval() 查看等间隔选取的行，或用 print_headtail() 查看开头和结尾。这些函数只缩短显示内容，仍保留完整的频数表。
code: lifeexp_tab <- lifeexp |>   transmute(region, lexp_70 = lexp >= 70)  tab(lifeexp_tab, region:lexp_70) #> # A tibble: 6 x 7 #>   region               lexp_70     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <dbl+lbl>            <lgl>   <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] FALSE      12   17.6   17.6 17.6       17.6 #> 2 1 [Europe & C. title: 从 Stata 到 R
text: 请将示例变量名替换为自己的变量。data 表示数据集，data1 和 data2 表示合并时的两份数据，fit 表示已拟合的模型。 R 标签注明主要使用的包。未加包名前缀的函数需要先加载相应包；许多数据准备示例 使用 library(dplyr)。findit() 本身不会加载或安装这些包。

title: 从 Stata 到 R
text: 与 Stata 有差异 表示默认设置、缺失值处理、估计方法或输出形式存在差异， 具体差异见注释。其余注释是使用提示。 执行核验检查 R 代码本身，并不证明结果与 Stata 数值一致。改写示例前，请核对 缺失值、权重、因子参照组、连接规则和标准误设置。搜索结果也不代表支持命令的全部选项。

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: small illustration adapts course survey, including deliberately missing centre show grouping works. tibble inputs, tab, summ, codebook variables families return tibbles, including tables inside lists. Base data frames data.table inputs retain respective table class supported. subclasses reconstructed newly shaped tables; data.table summaries retain keys indexes. corr(), pwcorr(), spearman(), misstable() duplicates_report() always return tibbles. Functions designed return vectors, ds() row_mean(), still return vectors.
code: library(dplyr) library(tibble) library(tidystata)  survey <- tibble(   centre = c("Riverside", "Riverside", "Hilltop", NA),   satisfied = c("Yes", NA, "No", "Yes"),   score = c(2, NA, 6, 8) )  survey |> tab(satisfied) #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   satisfied     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>     <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 No            1      25    25  33.3      33.3 #> 2 Yes           2      50    75  66.7     100   #> 3 NA            1      25   100  NA        NA

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Separate one-way tabulations return named list default. Extract table name: work one tibble instead, combine variable tables: Output options vary function: tab() .type argument. Multiple-pair explicitly grouped tab2()/fre2() calls still return lists: .type controls table inside. Correlations use .wide layout; layouts tibbles.
code: tables <- survey |> tab1(centre, satisfied)  tables[["satisfied"]] #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   value     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr> <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 No        1      25    25  33.3      33.3 #> 2 Yes       2      50    75  66.7     100   #> 3 NA        1      25   100  NA        NA survey |> tab1(centre, satisfied, .type = "tibble") #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   variable  value         n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>     <chr>     <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 centre    Hilltop       1      25    25  33.3      33.3 #> 2 centre    Riverside     2      50    75  66.7     100   #> 3 centre    NA            1      25   100  NA        NA   #> 4 satisfied No            1      25    25  33.3      33.3 #> 5 satisfied Yes           2      50    75  66.7     100   #> 6 satisfied NA            1      25   100  NA        NA

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: missing centre still group, make observed response invalid: one-way/joint tabulation summary families inherit group_by() groups unless .replaces . results ungrouped. Cross-tabulations require explicit .split group. summaries, .missing = FALSE drops missing grouping keys. Numeric calculations always omit missing measured values. Tabulation percentages use 0-100 scale, summary valid_pct uses 0-1. dedicated tab summ articles demonstrate denominators.
code: survey |> tab(satisfied, .by = centre) #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   centre    satisfied     n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>     <chr>     <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 Hilltop   No            1     100   100   100       100 #> 2 Riverside Yes           1      50    50   100       100 #> 3 Riverside NA            1      50   100    NA        NA #> 4 NA        Yes           1     100   100   100       100

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: empty input -missing measurement observed values. retain n = 0 undefined statistics, including sum = NA: Entirely missing summary columns emit warning. row sum follows different convention: adding observed items gives zero. row mean stays missing. Empty selections produce empty tabulation results; row helpers need least one column. Matrix columns unsupported tabulation column summaries.
code: survey |>   slice_head(n = 0) |>   summ(score, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean")) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   type      n   sum  mean #>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA tibble(item1 = c(NA_real_, 4), item2 = c(NA_real_, 6)) |>   mutate(     total = row_sum(pick(starts_with("item"))),     average = row_mean(pick(starts_with("item")))   ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   item1 item2 total average #>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1    NA    NA     0      NA #> 2     4     6    10       5

what: Understand labels and special missing values
title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: Variable labels describe columns; value labels describe particular codes. SPSS-style export might distinguish refusal unanswered question: Tabulations recognise ordinary, tagged SPSS user-missing values missing. Numeric summaries exclude calculations. decode() reads value labels, turn every labelled refusal ordinary NA. calculations outside haven-aware functions, explicitly normalise special missing values haven::zap_missing(). misstable() also accepts matrix nested data-frame columns. Ordinary list columns count scalar NA elements missing NULL observed. Structured columns use vctrs row-missingness rules; list-backed matrices different cell conventions, detailed missingness reference.
code: imported <- tibble(   answer = haven::labelled_spss(     c(1, 2, 99, NA),     labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2, Refused = 99),     na_values = 99,     label = "Course satisfaction"   ) )  imported |> fre(answer) #> # A tibble: 7 × 6 #>   answer            n percent   cum valid valid_cum #>   <chr>         <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 Yes               1      25    25    50        50 #> 2 No                1      25    50    50       100 #> 3 Valid Total       2      50    NA   100        NA #> 4 Refused           1      25    75    NA        NA #> 5 NA                1      25   100    NA        NA #> 6 Missing Total     2      50    NA    NA        NA #> 7 Total             4     100    NA    NA        NA

title: Containers, grouping and missing values
text: numeric calendar measurements occur together, default summaries separate type families. date table’s SD retains duration units: numeric table keeps numeric statistics. combined .type = "table" "tibble" output, shared location columns become character. Spread columns become plain numbers: days dates seconds date-times, units shown type.
code: visits <- tibble(   score = c(4, 8),   day = readr::parse_date(c("2026-09-01", "2026-09-03")) ) separate <- visits |> summ(.stat = c("n", "mean", "sd")) #> A list is returned as statistics are heterogeneous.  separate[["date"]] #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   name  type      n mean       sd            #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <chr>      <drtn>        #> 1 day   date      2 2026-09-02 1.414214 days

title: Getting started with tidystata
text: survey form uses -99 undisclosed income. Read numeric text, turn code NA, calculate average across two assessment items. Participant 2 one assessment answer, average uses answer. Participant 3 none: average NA answered zero. destring() also reads thousands separators; blank text becomes missing.
code: prepared <- survey |>   mutate(     income = destring(income_text) |> mvdecode(-99),     score = row_mean(pick(score1, score2)),     answered = row_non_miss(pick(score1, score2))   )  prepared |> select(id, income, score, answered) #> # A tibble: 12 × 4 #>       id income score answered #>    <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>    <int> #>  1     1   1200     3        2 #>  2     2   1500     4        1 #>  3     3     NA    NA        0 #>  4     4     NA     7        2 #>  5     5   2200     9        2 #>  6     6   1800     5        2 #>  7     7   1400     4        2 #>  8     8   2100     6        2 #>  9     9   2600     8        2 #> 10    10     NA     9        1 #> 11    11   2300     8        1 #> 12    12   1700     7        2

Use complete y,treat,x,z cases propensity scores [1e-5,1-1e-5]. treatment-weighted regression saturated, treat coefficient normalized weighted-cell mean difference (ATE). vcov="asympt" jointly accounts logit-estimated weights; summary reports robust z tests normal 95% confidence intervals. intercept target-population control mean. Stata reference · R reference IPW average treatment effect treated joint-estimation inference Stata R WeightIt Differs Stata Numeric binary treat: 0=control, 1=treated; continuous y; independent observations. Use complete y,treat,x,z cases propensity scores [1e-5,1-1e-5]. treatment-weighted regression saturated, treat coefficient normalized weighted-cell mean difference (ATT). vcov="asympt" jointly accounts logit-estimated weights; summary reports robust z tests normal 95% confidence intervals. intercept target-population control mean. IPW, without covariate adjustment weighted outcome regression. Stata reference · R reference
code: teffects ipw (y) (treat x z) { data <- data[stats::complete.cases(data[c("y", "treat", "x", "z")]), , drop = FALSE]; stopifnot(is.numeric(data$treat), setequal(unique(data$treat), c(0, 1))); w <- WeightIt::weightit(treat ~ x + z, data = data, method = "glm", link = "logit", estimand = "ATE", keep.mparts = TRUE); stopifnot(all(w$ps >= 1e-5 & w$ps <= 1 - 1e-5)); summary(WeightIt::lm_weightit(y ~ treat, data = data, weightit = w, vcov = "asympt"), ci = TRUE, level = .95) } teffects ipw (y) (treat x z) , atet { data <- data[stats::complete.cases(data[c("y", "treat", "x", "z")]), , drop = FALSE]; stopifnot(is.numeric(data$treat), setequal(unique(data$treat), c(0, 1))); w <- WeightIt::weightit(treat ~ x + z, data = data, method = "glm", link = "logit", estimand = "ATT", focal = 1, keep.mparts = TRUE); stopifnot(all(w$ps >= 1e-5 & w$ps <= 1 - 1e-5)); summary(WeightIt::lm_weightit(y ~ treat, data = data, weightit = w, vcov = "asympt"), ci = TRUE, level = .95) }

code: tsfilter bk cycle = y, minperiod(6) maxperiod(32) smaorder(12) { K <- 12; j <- -K:K; low <- 2 * pi / 32; high <- 2 * pi / 6; w <- ifelse(j == 0, (high - low) / pi, (sin(high * j) - sin(low * j)) / (pi * j)); w <- w - mean(w); stats::filter(y, w, sides = 2) } tsfilter hp cycle = y, smooth(1600) trend(trend) { n <- length(y); D <- diff(diag(n), differences = 2); trend <- drop(solve(diag(n) + 1600 * crossprod(D), as.numeric(y))); data.frame(trend = trend, cycle = as.numeric(y) - trend) }

text: MCMC有效样本量 Stata R coda 与 Stata 有差异 draws须为去除预热期的单条coda mcmc链。报告ESS、相关时间（抽样数/ESS）及效率（ESS/抽样数）。coda采用自回归谱估计，Stata采用截断样本自相关；诊断数值会有差异。 Stata 参考 · R 参考 后验均值标准差和分位数 Stata R posterior 与 Stata 有差异 draws须为包含参数后验抽样的coda mcmc或mcmc.list对象，例如MCMCpack::MCMCregress()的结果。报告均值、标准差、MCSE、中位数及95%等尾区间。MCSE算法与Stata不同。变换参数时须先变换抽样再汇总。 Stata 参考 · R 参考 变换系数的后验汇总 Stata R posterior 与 Stata 有差异 draws须为包含参数后验抽样的coda mcmc或mcmc.list对象，例如MCMCpack::MCMCregress()的结果。报告均值、标准差、MCSE、中位数及95%等尾区间。MCSE算法与Stata不同。变换参数时须先变换抽样再汇总。 Stata 参考 · R 参考 90%最高后验密度区间 Stata R posterior 与 Stata 有差异 draws为含x列的单条coda mcmc链。报告后验汇总及90%最短连续HPD区间，而非仅返回区间端点。多峰后验可能不存在单一HPD区间；MCSE算法与Stata不同。 Stata 参考 · R 参考

text: IPW平均处理效应及联合估计推断 Stata R WeightIt 与 Stata 有差异 数值型二元treat：0为对照、1为处理；y为连续结局；观测相互独立。使用y、treat、x、z完整案例，并要求倾向得分位于[1e-5,1-1e-5]。仅含处理指标的加权回归为饱和模型，其treat系数等于归一化加权组均值之差（ATE）。vcov="asympt"联合计入logit估计权重的不确定性；summary报告稳健z检验和正态95%置信区间。截距为目标人群的对照均值。这是IPW，未在加权结局回归中额外调整协变量。 Stata 参考 · R 参考 IPW处理组平均处理效应及联合估计推断 Stata R WeightIt 与 Stata 有差异 数值型二元treat：0为对照、1为处理；y为连续结局；观测相互独立。使用y、treat、x、z完整案例，并要求倾向得分位于[1e-5,1-1e-5]。仅含处理指标的加权回归为饱和模型，其treat系数等于归一化加权组均值之差（ATT）。vcov="asympt"联合计入logit估计权重的不确定性；summary报告稳健z检验和正态95%置信区间。截距为目标人群的对照均值。这是IPW，未在加权结局回归中额外调整协变量。 Stata 参考 · R 参考
code: teffects ipw (y) (treat x z) { data <- data[stats::complete.cases(data[c("y", "treat", "x", "z")]), , drop = FALSE]; stopifnot(is.numeric(data$treat), setequal(unique(data$treat), c(0, 1))); w <- WeightIt::weightit(treat ~ x + z, data = data, method = "glm", link = "logit", estimand = "ATE", keep.mparts = TRUE); stopifnot(all(w$ps >= 1e-5 & w$ps <= 1 - 1e-5)); summary(WeightIt::lm_weightit(y ~ treat, data = data, weightit = w, vcov = "asympt"), ci = TRUE, level = .95) } teffects ipw (y) (treat x z) , atet { data <- data[stats::complete.cases(data[c("y", "treat", "x", "z")]), , drop = FALSE]; stopifnot(is.numeric(data$treat), setequal(unique(data$treat), c(0, 1))); w <- WeightIt::weightit(treat ~ x + z, data = data, method = "glm", link = "logit", estimand = "ATT", focal = 1, keep.mparts = TRUE); stopifnot(all(w$ps >= 1e-5 & w$ps <= 1 - 1e-5)); summary(WeightIt::lm_weightit(y ~ treat, data = data, weightit = w, vcov = "asympt"), ci = TRUE, level = .95) }

Inference Pearson p-values use t = r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2)) n - 2 degrees freedom. unweighted data matches stats::cor.test(). Spearman ties receive average ranks, computed within sample used correlation. P-values test independence Stata 18 later : beta distribution fitted first four exact permutation moments statistic, normal approximation, sqrt(n - 1) * r, n = 3 valid fit exists. Earlier Stata versions stats::cor.test() use approximations, p-values can differ. constant variable gives NA, Stata's spearman reports correlation 1. k distinct variable pairs within group, Bonferroni Sidak adjustments min(1, k * p) min(1, 1 - (1 - p)^k), respectively. group's k includes pairs whose p-value NA; adjustment combine tests across groups. Stata options Stata's covariance, means, display-formatting options implemented. Use stats::cov() covariance summ() summaries. tidy long table R interface choice; Stata prints matrix. Display options star() print() also omitted: filter result instead, example dplyr::filter(p < 0.05).

title: Frequency tables and cross-tabulations — tab
text: Create Stata-style frequency tables using joint counts, separate one-way tables, pairwise cross-tabulations: tab(): Count combinations selected variables one long-format table frequencies percentages. fre(): Count combinations tab(), adding totals displaying value labels. tab1(): Tabulate variable separately, returning one-way frequency table variable. fre1(): Tabulate variable separately tab1(), adding totals displaying value labels. tab2(): Cross-tabulate every pair selected variables, returning wide contingency tables categories rows columns. fre2(): Cross-tabulate every pair tab2(), adding marginal totals displaying row-category labels. Column headers retain category codes.

Multiple pairs explicit .groups produce lists tables. two selected variables, tab() tab2() represent joint frequencies different layouts: tab() provides long table percentages, whereas tab2() shows cell counts two-way table. three variables, tab() counts joint combinations, tab2() produces separate table variable pair. title: Frequency tables and cross-tabulations — tab
text: Counts percentages following five columns produced tab(), tab1(), fre(), fre1(). group, let n_i count category (category combination) , N count across categories, N_valid count excluding observations missing measured variable. percentages 0–100 scale. n: Number observations category, sum weights weighted. percent: Percentage observations, 100 * n_i / N, including missing measured values denominator. cum: Cumulative percent, summed displayed category order. valid: Percentage complete observations, 100 * n_i / N_valid. NA categories missing measured values. valid_cum: Cumulative valid, displayed order, omitting missing measured categories. Thus percent corresponds Stata's tabulate, missing, valid uses denominator tabulate without missing. missing grouping key make measured value invalid. Missing values category order Missing measured values kept categories shown last. Missingness includes NA, NaN, tagged missing values, SPSS user-missing codes ranges; empty strings observed values. Factors follow level order; categories sorted value unless .desc requests frequency order. List-column elements counted complete values, flattened. Weighted counts percentages Let w_j weight observation j group. Frequency weights (.wt_type = "frequency"): Category counts n_i = sum(w_j) observations category. Weights need integers. Analytic weights (.wt_type = "analytic"): Weights rescaled within group sum number rows. Category counts sum rescaled weights, overall count stays sample-size scale. Percentages: weight types give percentages normalization factor cancels group. Cumulative valid percentages use corresponding weighted counts denominators. Rows missing weights excluded; negative weights allowed. ... omitted, weight column tabulated. Totals value labels fre() fre1() append "Total" row within group may add "Valid Total" "Missing Total" subtotals. fre2() adds marginal total row column. fre() fre1() display value labels; fre2() displays row-category labels keeps column headers based category codes. tab() tab1() retain underlying category codes types. Totals may convert category column character introduce total label column. Distinct category codes remain separate even labels coincide. Cross-tabulations association tests tab2() fre2() report cell counts rather five percentages listed . .chi2 = TRUE, Pearson's chi-square test uses displayed categories, including missing ones. Filter missing categories beforehand contribute test. Empty rows columns excluded calculation. Let O_ij observed cell count, E_ij expected count independence, r number nonempty rows, c number nonempty columns, N total count: Expected counts: E_ij = row_total_i * column_total_j / N. Pearson's chi-square: X^2 = sum((O_ij - E_ij)^2 / E_ij). Degrees freedom: df = (r - 1) * (c - 1). p-value: Upper-tail probability chi-square distribution df degrees freedom. Cramer's V: sqrt(X^2 / (N * min(r - 1, c - 1))). 2--2 tables, signed phi coefficient, Stata, sign O_11 * O_22 - O_12 * O_21. Frequency weights act cell counts test. Analytic weights supported; complex survey designs, use survey::svychisq(). Cross-tabulation category values become column names, conflicts reserved names "total" may require recoding. Computed variables groups Named expressions ... evaluated ungrouped data, counts calculated within groups. Use grouped dplyr::mutate() first group-specific computations. Input column names conflict output columns renamed result; input data unchanged.
